contentBlocks.text: SASSA Appeal Timeline: How Long Does an Appeal Take?

Understanding the appeal timeline helps you plan and avoid unnecessary follow-ups. The Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA) has specific timeframes for each stage of the process.
This guide is for anyone who has submitted an appeal with ITSAA and wants to understand how long each stage of the process takes.
After you submit your appeal on the ITSAA portal, you will receive an acknowledgment SMS or email within 5-10 business days confirming receipt.
The tribunal reviews your case and may request additional documentation if needed. This stage takes 2-4 weeks.
A final ruling is issued within 60-90 days from the date of submission. Complex cases involving fraud flags or medical evidence may take up to 120 days.

contentBlocks.title: Full Timeline
contentBlocks.text: The full appeal process takes 60 to 90 days from submission to final ruling. Complex cases involving fraud flags or medical evidence may take up to 120 days.

items: Appeal reference number for tracking purposes
Copy of the original decline notification from SASSA
Any supporting evidence uploaded with your appeal
Ruling in your favour within 60-90 days — backdated payments issued within 2 weeks
Ruling against you — you may reapply for the grant fresh if your circumstances change

faqs.question: Can I speed up the appeal process?
faqs.answer: No, but submitting complete documentation upfront avoids delays from follow-up requests. Calling the tribunal will not accelerate the review.

faqs.question: Do I get paid during the appeal process?
faqs.answer: No. Payments only resume if and when your appeal is approved, at which point you receive backpay to the original decline date.
